trades.note: Buy 09:00 -> sell 15:00 at the SAME price, net 0. Block derivation and grouping run on visible data only and produce what looks like a completely ordinary closed flat trade. Nothing about the trade record itself signals a problem — that's the trap this fixture is built to catch.

sync.blocking_reason_note: The gap window [10:00Z, 14:00Z) falls strictly inside trade_1's [opened_at 09:00Z, closed_at 15:00Z). Per Module 02 §4.6 ('assert no coverage_gap overlaps this server_day') and §6.3 ('a day is never marked closable while a coverage gap exists in it'), server_day 2026-08-10 must never be closeable while this gap remains unresolved, even though the visible trade looks clean.
sync.scoping_note: This models the gap as arising from a missed SCHEDULED sync (00-foundation §7.3's alerting condition: sync_run_2's window starts at 14:00Z instead of continuing from sync_run_1's 10:00Z end) rather than the WITHIN-run 'gap between window_from and the earliest returned fill' mechanism described in Module 02 §4.1 step 5. Both are coverage_gaps rows in the end, but they're detected by different reconciliation logic (schedule-vs-actual-runs, vs. within-a-run feed completeness) — worth being explicit about so this fixture isn't read as testing §4.1 step 5 specifically.

invariant_checks.invariant: a day is never closable while a coverage gap exists in it (Module 02 §6.3, §4.6)
sum of fill P&L equals trade P&L (00-foundation §9.2)
